# Go reference fixtures

These files were written by the Go version of spela, through its own code, so
the Rust migration and parity tests can check against what Go really wrote.
They are generated by `tools/goref`. Do not edit them by hand; change the
generator and run it again:

```bash
GOPROXY=off GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go run ./tools/goref fixtures
```

## Layout

Each case is a folder that mirrors the XDG homes Go wrote into:

- `config/spela/` is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/spela`: config.yaml, profiles/, lists/.
- `data/spela/` is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/spela`: games.yaml, backups/.
- `cache/spela/` is `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/spela`: manifest.json, update-check.json.
- `home/` is `$HOME`, used by the sandboxes for the fixture Steam install.
- `library/` folders hold fixture game files and Steam libraries.
- `oracle.json` (where present) is what Go made of the case when it read it
  back: effective values, origins, load errors. It is not a Go file; goref
  wrote it from Go's return values.

## Paths

Go writes absolute paths. Every text file here has the case folder replaced by
the token `/fixture-root`. A test copies a case into a temp folder and
replaces `/fixture-root` with that folder in every text file before use.

The sha256 in a backup file name such as `<sha256>-nvngx_dlss.dll` is the
hash Go computes over the original path. goref renames these files after the
copy so the hash is taken over the path under `/fixture-root`, as if Go had
run there; that keeps the names stable between runs. After a test relocates a
case the names no longer match a fresh hash. Go never recomputes the name of
an existing entry (restore uses the recorded `backup_path`), so tests must not
either.

## Times

Times that a caller can choose are pinned to 2026-10-26T17:02:10.123456789+02:00
(a deliberate non-UTC offset). Go always stamps `games.yaml` `updated_at`
and the manifest cache `fetched_at` with the clock, so those change on each
run.

## Fictional games

Fixture games and app ids are fictional (9100010 to 9100499), decision 43. Where
a Go test or the Go e2e harness pins a real game, the case keeps the test's
shape with a fictional name and id. Real ids appear only where they come from
Go's built-in deny list, because a check against that list needs one of its
entries.

## Files

| Path | What it covers | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `backups/basename-names/` | The older scheme where the backup file is the plain basename, as TestLegacyBasenameBackupMetadataRestores writes it; the game holds a newer swapped DLL | `dll.SaveBackup` |
| `backups/custom-backup-path/` | `backup_path` set in config.yaml: backup files sit under it while `backup.json` stays in `data/spela/backups/<appid>/` | `(*Config).Save`, `dll.CreateBackup`, `dll.SaveBackup` |
| `backups/invalid-index/` | Backup indexes Go's LoadBackup refuses: wrong app id, no files, an empty path, JSON that does not parse | `json.MarshalIndent` of `dll.Backup` (SaveBackup's encoder) into the index path; the last one literal |
| `backups/mixed-names/` | One index with a basename entry and a sha256 entry that CreateBackup added later; the first backup of a path is kept | `dll.SaveBackup`, then `dll.CreateBackup` |
| `backups/sha256-names/` | `backup.json` and backup files named `<sha256 of the original path>-<basename>`, two of them with the same basename in different folders, and the game install they came from | `dll.CreateBackup`, then `dll.SaveBackup` to pin `created_at` |
| `caches/manifest-with-fetch-time/` | Manifest cache with `fetched_at` and `source_url`, from the repository's data/manifest.json | `dll.SaveManifest` |
| `caches/manifest-without-fetch-time/` | A manifest cache from before `fetched_at` and `source_url` (Go then uses the file time and the default URL) | `json.MarshalIndent` of `dll.Manifest`, Go's cache encoder |
| `caches/update-check/` | `update-check.json` after a check that found v0.7.0 (`update-check.ok.json`) and after a failed first check, which has no `latest` (`update-check.failed.json`); rename either to `update-check.json` to use it | `release.Check` against a loopback test server |
| `config/broken/` | A config.yaml that does not parse; the oracle holds Go's error | literal YAML, read by `config.Load` |
| `config/default/` | Default config as Go saves it; shader_cache is the computed `<cache>/nvidia` | `config.Default()`, `(*Config).Save` |
| `config/every-key/` | Every config key set away from its default, including `theme`, `compact_mode`, a two-entry library path list with a space | `(*Config).Save` |
| `config/explicit-zeros/` | Explicit empty and zero values: `shader_cache: ""`, `log_level: ""`, `manifest_refresh_hours: 0`, and the `omitempty` keys Go leaves out | `(*Config).Save` |
| `config/partial/` | Hand-written config with only two keys and 2-space indentation; the oracle shows the defaults Go fills in | literal YAML, read by `config.Load` |
| `config/retired-keys/` | Retired `show_hints` and `preferred_dll_source`, an unknown key, `theme: light` and an unknown log level `verbose` | literal YAML (Go's struct cannot write these keys), read by `config.Load` |
| `config/wrong-type/` | A config value of the wrong type (`manifest_refresh_hours: daily`) | literal YAML, read by `config.Load` |
| `e2e/library/` | The Go e2e harness's three-game library in fictional form (Chrome Avenue 2081 with DLSS and DLSS-G 3.7.0, Hollow Crown 3 with DLSS 3.5.0, Ashen Throne with none), config.yaml, a default.yaml with no overrides key, 9100110.yaml and manifest.json | a copy of `setupTestEnvironment` in `tests/e2e/mock_helper.go` (yaml.v3 `Marshal` of the same maps) with fictional names and app ids (decision 43), times pinned |
| `games/database/` | `games.yaml` with DLLs of every family and versions in each formatter shape (2, 3 and 4 parts), a DLL with no readable version and an upper-case name, games with and without a prefix, Steam tools that old scans kept, a name with a colon and an apostrophe, local and UTC times, and the fixture game folders with PE stubs | `game.Transaction`, `(*Database).AddGame`, `dll.ScanDirectory` |
| `lists/denylist-user/` | A user `denylist.yaml` (Go never writes it; it replaces the built-in list in Go) next to an overrides file | yaml.v3 `Marshal` of `denylist.DenyList`; overrides by `denylist.Deny` |
| `lists/overrides-empty/` | Empty `overrides.yaml` as Go writes it (`allowed: []`, `denied: []`) | `denylist.SaveOverrides` |
| `lists/overrides-full/` | `overrides.yaml` with a force-allowed built-in game, user denials (one with a numeric name, as `denylist deny` writes for an unknown id), and one game in both lists | `denylist.Allow`, `denylist.Deny` |
| `profiles/broken-default/` | A `default.yaml` that does not parse: the legacy game profile fails with it, the one with an overrides map still loads | literal YAML |
| `profiles/broken-yaml/` | Game profiles that do not load: unparseable YAML, a wrong type, duplicate keys, tab indentation; `profile.List` skips them | literal YAML; valid sibling by `profile.Mutate` |
| `profiles/default-no-overrides-key/` | A `default.yaml` with no `overrides` key at all (as the Go e2e fixture writes it) | literal YAML; game by `profile.Mutate` |
| `profiles/default-unmarked/` | All games with set values and no markers (`overrides: {}`), which Go counts as set when non-zero; `smt: false` counts as set | `profile.SaveDefault`, `profile.Mutate` |
| `profiles/dropped-fields/` | Every field decision 10 drops (8 overlay fields, `gpu.power_mizer`, `cpu.affinity`) set in a game and some in All games, plus non-zero `clock_offset` and `memory_offset` (decision 31) | `profile.Mutate`, `profile.MutateDefault`, `(*Profile).Set` |
| `profiles/every-field/` | Every one of the 35 fields set and marked, in All games (a mix of zero and non-zero values) and in one game (the values of Go's YAML contract test), 4-space indentation | `profile.MutateDefault`, `profile.Mutate`, `(*Profile).Set` |
| `profiles/explicit-zeros/` | A game with every field marked and every value zero (`smt` nil, so marked with no value), against All games with non-zero values | `profile.Save`, `profile.MutateDefault` |
| `profiles/file-names/` | File names Go's List and Load treat differently: `.yml`, a leading zero stem, a non-numeric stem, `default.yml`, a text file | literal YAML; valid profile by `profile.Mutate` |
| `profiles/invalid-in-go/` | Values Go's setters refuse and Go loads anyway: `sr_mode: ultra`, `rr_mode: Quality` and `multi_frame` 6 and 8, plus relative `shader_cache_path` values, in All games and two games (decision 65) | `profile.Save`, `profile.SaveDefault` (only `(*Profile).Set` checks the lists) |
| `profiles/invalid-vrr/` | An invalid `gpu.vrr` in a game and a wrongly cased one in `default.yaml`: Go fails to load both | literal YAML; valid sibling by `profile.Mutate` |
| `profiles/legacy-go-test-clock/` | Go test TestLoad_FileWithoutOverridesKeyStillMigrates: legacy clock offset equal to the default, fan speed different | the Go test's YAML with a fictional app id and name in place of its real ones (decision 43); default by `profile.SaveDefault` |
| `profiles/legacy-go-test-hdr/` | Go test TestMigration_LegacyProfileRoundTrip: a 2-space legacy profile (no `overrides` key) against a default with values | the Go test's YAML with a fictional app id and name in place of its real ones (decision 43); default by `profile.SaveDefault` |
| `profiles/legacy-no-default/` | The same legacy game profile with no `default.yaml`: every non-zero value becomes an own value | literal YAML in the shape Go wrote before the overrides map |
| `profiles/legacy-with-default/` | A 4-space legacy game profile (no `overrides` key) with `vrr: unset`, `smt: false`, non-zero clock and memory offsets and dropped fields, against a legacy `default.yaml` with values | literal YAML in the shape Go wrote before the overrides map |
| `profiles/markers/` | `false` markers, unknown marker keys (`made.up`, `overlay.bogus`) and a `false` `dlss.sr_model_preset` marker, in All games and a game | `profile.Save`, `profile.SaveDefault` with a hand-built overrides map |
| `profiles/migrated-go-test/` | Go test TestMigration_SkipsAlreadyMigrated: a 2-space profile with an `overrides` map pinning `vkd3d_heap: false` against a default of true | the Go test's YAML with a fictional app id and name in place of its real ones (decision 43); default by `profile.SaveDefault` |
| `profiles/overrides-empty-map/` | `overrides: {}` with stored leaves that have no marker (no effect in Go), and an empty profile with only a name | `profile.Save`, `profile.SaveDefault` |
| `profiles/own-values/` | Own values with explicit zeros and `smt: false` that differ from All games, and own values equal to All games or to the system default (`this_game_same`) | `profile.Mutate`, `profile.MutateDefault`, `(*Profile).Set` |
| `profiles/sr-model-preset/` | The retired `dlss.sr_model_preset` key and marker in All games and games, a legacy file with only that key, and a lowercase `sr_preset: k` | literal YAML (Go no longer writes `sr_model_preset`) |
| `profiles/two-space/` | 2-space indented `default.yaml` and game profile with an overrides map, as Go's tests write them by hand | literal YAML, read by `profile.Load` |
| `profiles/yaml-shapes/` | Shapes yaml.v3 loads that a strict reader refuses: floats in int fields (`power_limit: 250.0`, `fan_speed: 40.7`, cut toward zero) and a second `---` document, which yaml.v3 ignores | literal YAML, read by `profile.Load` |
| `profiles/yaml11-bools/` | YAML 1.1 booleans: `smt: yes`, `on`, `off`, `Yes`, `y`, `TRUE`, `NO`, also as a marker value | literal YAML, read by `profile.Load` |
| `sandbox/empty/` | An empty home with no Steam install and no spela files, for empty-state transcripts | nothing; Go writes only what the commands create |
| `sandbox/errors/` | The main sandbox plus a game profile that does not parse (9100030) and one with an invalid `gpu.vrr` (9100060), for error transcripts | as `sandbox/main`, plus literal YAML |
| `sandbox/main/` | The transcript sandbox: a fixture Steam install under `home/.steam/steam` plus `library2` (two libraries, PE stub DLLs, prefixes, a tool, a game with a pending update, compat tools and config.vdf), config.yaml with rescans, update checks and manifest refresh off and a loopback manifest URL, a seeded manifest cache, games.yaml from Go's own scan, All games and four game profiles, deny overrides and one backup | `steam.ScanLibraries`, `game.Transaction`, `(*Config).Save`, `profile.Mutate`, `profile.MutateDefault`, `profile.Create`, `denylist.Deny`, `denylist.Allow`, `dll.CreateBackup`; Steam files and the manifest cache are hand-built |

## Transcripts

`transcripts/` holds the output of the read-only Go commands run against the
sandbox cases. See `transcripts/COMMANDS.md`.
